notice: RN bank batch 134: Mental health case studies: olanzapine and tardive dyskinesia, valproate and lamotrigine, GAD and smoking cessation, with four standalone items. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md. Also carries the bank-wide catalog (catalog.py): the RN Question Bank and every curated test set.

questions.stem: A client on a surgical unit has new problems on day 3. Using the note, fill in the bowtie: the most likely condition in the middle, two actions to take now on the left and two parameters to monitor on the right.

actions.text: Apply four-point restraints as the very first step to protect the staff
Give haloperidol alone for the hallucinations
Withhold IV fluids to prevent fluid overload

rationale.correct: Delirium tremens needs benzodiazepines, thiamine and close monitoring.

perOption.c1: Day 3, confusion, hallucinations, fever and autonomic overactivity.
perOption.c2: No eye signs; marked autonomic overactivity points to withdrawal.
perOption.c3: Does not explain hallucinations and fever.
perOption.c4: Would cause slow breathing and pinpoint pupils.
perOption.a4: Lowers seizure threshold and does not treat withdrawal.

references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize and act on delirium tremens.

exhibits.title: Day 3 after a hip fracture repair
exhibits.body: Drinks a bottle of wine daily (told the team on day 2). Now confused, picking at the air, seeing insects on the wall. T 38.6 C, HR 132/min, BP 172/98, drenched in sweat, coarse tremor.

questions.stem: A client in alcohol withdrawal has CIWA-Ar scores every 2 hours on a symptom-triggered protocol (lorazepam for scores of 10 or more). For each time, choose the action.

options.text: Give lorazepam per protocol and reassess in 1 hour
No medicine; reassess in 4 hours
Call a code
No dose; reassess per protocol
Give lorazepam anyway
Stop all monitoring
Hold benzodiazepines and notify the provider
Give lorazepam
Encourage a walk

rationale.correct: Symptom-triggered dosing treats high scores and watches for oversedation.
references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: In a psychiatric emergency service, four clients arrive within 10 minutes. Which client should the nurse assess first?

options.text: A client with schizophrenia who says the voices are back but is calm and asking for a sandwich
A client who took an unknown number of acetaminophen tablets 3 hours ago and says, "I'm fine now"
A client with panic disorder who is breathing fast, clutching the chest and saying, "I'm dying"
A client with bipolar disorder who is loud, pacing and demanding to see the doctor right now

rationale.correct: An acetaminophen overdose looks well early but is time-critical.

perOption.b: A potentially fatal overdose that looks well early; the antidote works best within 8 hours.
perOption.c: Distressing but rarely dangerous; check vital signs soon.
perOption.d: Needs limits but is not in danger.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: A client admitted voluntarily for depression asks to leave the unit today. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Tell the client of the right to request discharge

Tell the client that voluntary clients can never leave without a court order
Lock the client's belongings away until the client changes their mind

caseStudies.title: Olanzapine with metabolic syndrome and tardive dyskinesia

exhibits.title: Early psychosis clinic
exhibits.body: A 24-year-old client with first-episode schizophrenia has taken olanzapine 20 mg daily for 9 months. Voices are mostly gone, but the client often forgets doses and was readmitted once. The parent notices lip smacking and tongue movements. The client says, "I'm always hungry."

caseStudies.title: Bipolar disorder on valproate and lamotrigine with a severe rash

exhibits.title: Mood disorders clinic
exhibits.body: A 30-year-old client with bipolar I disorder takes valproate 1,000 mg twice daily. Lamotrigine was added 3 weeks ago for depressive episodes, and the dose was raised quickly last week. The client hopes to become pregnant next year. Today the client has a fever, a spreading rash and sore lips.

rows.label: Skin
cells: Red-purple patches on the trunk with blisters

caseStudies.title: Generalized anxiety disorder with SSRI discontinuation and buspirone

exhibits.title: Primary care
exhibits.body: A 41-year-old client with generalized anxiety disorder stopped paroxetine 3 days ago without telling anyone because of weight gain. The client now has dizziness, "electric shock" feelings in the head, nausea, irritability and vivid dreams.

exhibits.title: Primary care
exhibits.body: A 48-year-old client with depression (stable on sertraline) and COPD smokes 25 cigarettes a day and wants to quit. The client has tried nicotine gum before and relapsed after 2 weeks. The client smokes the first cigarette within 5 minutes of waking.

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
